descriptionChirho: To seek or search for someone or something, whether physically or metaphorically (Qal active, Arabic طَلَبَ 'talaba' = to seek/request); the primary and most frequent sense of darash.
To inquire of God or a prophet, to consult an oracle or divine authority for guidance (Qal, Arabic سَأَلَ 'sa'ala' = to ask/inquire); a specialized sense of seeking divine direction.
To require or demand something, especially blood or accountability; to call to account for wrongdoing (Qal, Arabic أَطْلُبُ / أُطَالِبُ = I demand/require); a juridical and covenantal sense.
To investigate, examine, or search out a matter thoroughly (Qal, Arabic بَحَثَ 'bahatha' / فَحَصَ 'fahasa' = to investigate/examine); careful judicial or intellectual inquiry.
To seek the welfare of, to care for or attend to someone or something (Qal, Arabic يَعْتَنِي 'ya'tani' = to care for); a figurative extension where seeking becomes tending.
To allow oneself to be consulted or sought; to be inquired of, especially said of God permitting or refusing inquiry (Niphal passive/reflexive, Arabic أُسْتَشَارُ / سُئِلْتُ = to be consulted/asked).

labelChirho: be required, be sought out (Niphal passive)
descriptionChirho: To be required or demanded; to be sought out as a passive state (Niphal participle/passive, Arabic مَطْلُوبٌ 'matloob' = required/demanded).
